title: Pizza Dough

ingredients.title: Ingredients
items: 500 g (3 ¾ cups) Italian “00” flour (ideal for pizza; substitute bread flour if unavailable)
325 ml (1 ⅓ cups + 1 tbsp) cold water
2 g (½ tsp) fresh yeast (or 1 g dry yeast — very little is used for slow fermentation)
15 ml (1 tbsp) extra virgin olive oil (optional, for tenderness)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Mixing
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the cold water.
Add about 10% of the flour and mix to form a slurry.
Gradually incorporate the remaining flour and salt until the dough comes together.
Knead by hand (15 min) or mixer (8 min, low speed) until smooth and elastic.
The dough should be soft, slightly tacky, but not sticky.

instruction.title: Step 2 – First Rest (Bulk Fermentation)
steps: Shape into a ball, cover, and rest at room temperature for 1 hour.
This slow cold fermentation develops deep flavor and digestibility.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Portioning & Proofing
steps: Remove from fridge, divide into 4 equal dough balls (~200–220 g each).
Shape tightly into balls, place in a floured tray or covered box.
Let rise at room temperature 4–6 hours until doubled, soft, and airy.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Stretching & Baking
steps: If possible, use a pizza stone or steel preheated for at least 45 min.
Lightly flour the surface, press dough gently from the center outward — do not use a rolling pin.
This preserves the airy cornicione (puffy crust).
Top with high-quality Italian ingredients (San Marzano tomatoes, mozzarella di bufala, fresh basil, drizzle of olive oil).
Home oven (with stone/steel): Bake for 6–8 minutes.
Professional wood-fired oven (450–480 °C): Bake for 60–90 seconds.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Top with your favorite pizza sauce, cheese, and fresh toppings before baking.
Best baked on a preheated pizza stone or steel for an authentic crust.

chefTips: Flour: Italian “00” with high W value (280–320) gives elasticity and chew.
Water: Cold water slows fermentation and strengthens gluten.
Yeast: Minimal yeast, long fermentation = better flavor and digestibility.
Hydration: This recipe is ~65% hydration (water-to-flour ratio) for softness and airy texture.
Fermentation: 24–48 hours cold ferment is the secret to top pizzerias.
